conversation.content: When can I enroll in Medicare and select my coverage? And when can I make changes to my coverage after I've enrolled?

### Initial Enrollment in Medicare
Medicare eligibility typically begins at age 65 (or earlier if you have certain disabilities or End-Stage Renal Disease). Your **Initial Enrollment Period (IEP)** is the first chance to sign up without penalties. It's a **7-month window**:
- **3 months before** the month you turn 65.
- **The month** you turn 65.
- **3 months after** the month you turn 65.

**Key actions during IEP:**
- **Part A (Hospital Insurance)**: Automatic for most if you've paid Medicare taxes for 10+ years (premium-free). Otherwise, enroll and pay a premium.
- **Part B (Medical Insurance)**: Enroll voluntarily (monthly premium required). Coverage starts the first of the month after enrollment (or sooner if you sign up early).
- **Part C (Medicare Advantage)** or **Part D (Prescription Drugs)**: You can join these during IEP if offered in your area.

If you miss IEP and don't have qualifying group health coverage (e.g., from work), you'll face lifelong late enrollment penalties (higher premiums).

**Special Enrollment Period (SEP):** If you're 65+ and covered by employer/group health plan (or spouse's), you get an 8-month SEP starting the month after that coverage ends or employment ends—**no penalties**.

For official details: [Medicare.gov Eligibility](https://www.medicare.gov/basics/get-started-with-medicare/sign-up/when-can-i-sign-up-for-medicare).

### Selecting Coverage (Parts C and D)
- During your IEP, you can choose a Medicare Advantage (Part C) plan or standalone Part D drug plan.
- Outside IEP, use the **Annual Enrollment Period (AEP)**: **October 15 – December 7** each year. Changes take effect January 1.

### Making Changes After Enrollment
You can't change anytime—use these periods to switch, drop, or add coverage:

| Period | Dates | What You Can Do |
|--------|-------|-----------------|
| **Annual Enrollment Period (AEP)** | Oct 15 – Dec 7 | Switch from Original Medicare to Advantage (or vice versa), change Advantage plans, join/switch/drop Part D. Affects Jan 1. |
| **Medicare Advantage Open Enrollment (OEP)** | Jan 1 – Mar 31 (if enrolled in Advantage) | Switch Advantage plans, return to Original Medicare + optional Part D. One change per period; affects next month. |
| **Special Enrollment Periods (SEP)** | Varies (2–12 months) | Qualifying events like moving, losing employer coverage, marriage/divorce, etc. Check eligibility for penalty-free changes. |
| **Trial Right** (Advantage only) | First 12 months in plan | Leave anytime for Original Medicare + Part D. |
| **General Enrollment** (last resort) | Jan 1 – Mar 31 | Enroll in Parts A/B only (penalties apply); coverage starts July 1. |

**Tips:**
- Use Medicare's Plan Finder tool at [Medicare.gov/plan-compare](https://www.medicare.gov/plan-compare) during open periods.
- Late changes often incur penalties (e.g., 1% per month late for Part B/D).
- SHIP counselors offer free, unbiased help: Call 1-800-MEDICARE (1-800-633-4227) or find local help at [ShipHelp.org](https://www.shiphelp.org).

Rules can vary by situation—verify with Medicare.gov or SSA.gov for your specifics.
